evidence_quotes.agenda: 'What are your biggest concerns on your move?' — asked right after confirming the date, before any logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer named her mother's 20-year-old China cabinet as her single biggest worry, and the rep tracked it specifically across the whole call — confirming it needed extra care, later identifying a second similar heirloom piece she'd nearly left out, and reassuring her explicitly that 'this is your mother's important item, so we'll definitely secure that.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: None of the 5 lines reached — no rate-commit line, no restated estimate-variability framing, no explicit pay-less-if-faster line, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' check.

top_strength: Genuinely attentive, sustained care around the emotional core of the call — the mother's antique China cabinet — plus flexible problem-solving on an unusual add-on stop (picking up a washer/dryer from a storage unit en route).
coaching_note: A great discovery-stage call that thins out in Stage 3 — none of the Save Your Ass lines landed and the close never got a formal ask, though that's partly because she'd already told the rep her mother is the actual decision-maker. Total rounded from a raw component sum of 67.5 (half-point from a Stage 2 split).
